extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy analysts, and other users of USPTO patent prosecution data (empirical researchers, patent scholars, economists, and policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation describing variables, coding rules, and limitations for the USPTO Office Action Research Dataset (office_actions, rejections, citations) covering Non‑Final and Final rejections (2008–2017). Intended to guide dataset users in interpreting and merging these files for empirical research on patent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Number (app_id)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application received by the USPTO is given a unique application number (app_id). The number is eight digits long and used to keep track of the application while it is being processed and examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first two digits indicate the application's series number (for non‑PCT filings). This release includes Office actions for series 12, 13, 14, and 15. Use app_id to link observations across files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image File Wrapper (IFW) Number (ifw_number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Office action issued by the USPTO is given an Image File Wrapper (IFW) identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ifw_number is a unique, alpha‑numeric code that serves as the primary key for linking observations across the three data files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Code (document_cd)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Office action has a document code identifying the type of document issued by the examiner to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This release includes CTNF (Non‑Final Rejection) and CTFR (Final Rejection). CTNF rejects claims but does not close prosecution and can include objections/requirements. CTFR is made final, may include grounds for objections/rejections/requirements, and limits applicant’s amendment rights (only canceling claims or complying with a prior formal requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail Date (mail_dt)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mail_dt variable is the date the Office action was mailed‑out from USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mail date indicates action timing and is important because the impact of an Office action depends on the stage of prosecution when issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Art Unit (art_unit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The art_unit variable indicates the group art unit to which the examiner issuing the Office action belongs (four digit number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first two digits indicate the technology center (TC). The documentation lists TC codes (e.g., 1600 Biotechnology; 1700 Chemical; 2100 Computer Architecture/Software; etc.). Use art_unit for technology routing and cross‑sectional analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification Codes (uspc_class / uspc_subclass)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO assigns a primary US Patent Classification (USPC) class and subclass for routing and prior art searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although USPTO transitioned toward CPC after 2013, the dataset captures USPC (relevant for examiner assignment). Use uspc_class/uspc_subclass for analysis of technology classes; other tools (PatentsView) can provide CPC/IPCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heading Structure Missing (header_missing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that identifies when the Office action does not include standard headings or contains no headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO recommends examiners use a standardized Office action template with headings to improve consistency and readability. header_missing flags deviations from that template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Paragraph Missing (fp_missing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that identifies when the Office action does not contain the standard form paragraph(s) for the rejection(s) raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard form paragraphs contain relevant legal definitions and provide for a streamlined and consistent format. Missing form paragraphs may complicate automated categorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection and Form Paragraph Mismatch (rejection_fp_mismatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that identifies when the form paragraph(s) included in the Office action do not match the rejection(s) raised in the action sentence(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This flags cases where heading/form‑paragraph analysis disagrees with NPL sentence‑structure analysis of the action text; useful for quality checks and manual validation (see variable definition in Section IVa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing Paragraph Missing (closing_missing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator that identifies if contact information (phone number, alternative contact) is missing from the closing paragraph of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO expects specific contact information at the end of the Office action; closing_missing flags when that closing paragraph is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 101 Rejection (rejection_101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether a 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection is raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, an examiner rejects under 101 if any of four requirements is not met: (1) no statutory double patenting (one patent per inventor/discovery), (2) inventor identification requirements (pre/post Sept 16, 2012 rules), (3) claimed invention falls within patent‑eligible categories (process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter) as interpreted by courts, and (4) claimed invention is useful (specific, substantial, credible). If a 101 rejection appears, it is further categorized into subtypes based on form paragraphs and triggering keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 102 Rejection (rejection_102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether a 35 U.S.C. 102 rejection (lack of novelty) is raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner rejects as anticipated if claim is expressly or inherently described by a single prior art reference. When present, 102 rejections are specified into subtypes based on statute paragraphs (e.g., 102(a), 102(b), pre‑AIA vs AIA mappings).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection (rejection_103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection (obviousness) is raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner rejects as obvious if the claimed invention would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art and must provide objective evidence. 103 rejections are further specified into subtypes (principally 103(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112 Rejection (rejection_112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether a 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection is raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner rejects under 112 when requirements regarding adequacy of disclosure are not met (written description, indefiniteness, enablement). Subtypes map to paragraph labels (112(a), 112(b), etc.), and pre‑AIA paragraphs are mapped to post‑AIA alphabetical equivalents for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑statutory Double Patenting Rejection (rejection_dp)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether a non‑statutory double patenting rejection is raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑statutory double patenting generally occurs when similar (but not identical) scope is claimed by a common inventor and/or assignee. (See MPEP 804 for comprehensive discussion.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection (objection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether an objection is raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections are generally raised for minor informalities or violations of patent rules (e.g., claims not properly grouped, figure elements not properly referenced). Reference: 37 C.F.R. 1.75(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable Claims (allowed_claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates when the Office action includes text specifying that one or more claims are allowable if the objection can be overcome, or that certain claims are allowed without any objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use allowed_claims to identify claim‑level allowances or contingent allowances within Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater Than One Citation in 102 Rejection (cite102_gt1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates when more than one reference is cited as the basis to reject certain claim(s) under 35 U.S.C. 102 in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may include definitional or evidentiary references even when rejection is based on a single citation; cite102_gt1 flags multiple references used for 102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greater Than Three Citations in 103 Rejection (cite103_gt3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates when more than three references are cited as the basis to reject certain claim(s) under 35 U.S.C. 103 in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for distinguishing dense prior art bases for obviousness rejections across technology areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: One Citation in 103 Rejection (cite103_eq1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates when only one reference is cited as the basis to reject certain claim(s) under 35 U.S.C. 103 in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that examiners may rely on established knowledge or 'Examiner’s official notice' to support a 103 rejection based on a single citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Max Citations in 103 Rejection (cite103_max)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates the largest number of references cited as the basis to reject certain claim(s) under 35 U.S.C. 103 in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, the maximum number across claims in an action. Caution: algorithm can overcount when non‑patent literature with individual author names or chemical codes are present, especially in NPL‑heavy tech areas; planned improvements noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature Type (signature_type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates the signature types of the Office action based on examiner titles extracted from the signature block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values: 0 – Examiner; 1 – Primary Examiner (PE); 2 – Examiner + PE; 3 – Examiner + Supervisory Patent Examiner (SPE); 4 – Examiner + PE/SPE + Director. Use to characterize who signed the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Type (action_type)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground for rejection raised in the Office action, action_type indicates the relevant section of 35 U.S.C. or relevant categories where statutory sections do not apply (e.g., non‑statutory double patenting, objections, allowed claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: action_type is the key variable linking document actions to statutory grounds and is used together with action_subtype to form document‑action observations in the rejections file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Subtype (action_subtype)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each grounds for rejection raised in the Office action, action_subtype indicates the paragraph letter within the relevant section of 35 U.S.C. and contains categories where paragraphs do not apply (principally 101 subtypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtypes appear in the rejections file. Because AIA amended certain sections, 102 subtypes may have different meanings pre‑ and post‑AIA; the dataset maps pre‑AIA paragraphs to post‑AIA equivalents for 112 and provides labels for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Rejected (claim_numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim_numbers field lists the application claims in question for each action (action_type/action_subtype combination) raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use claim_numbers to map document‑action pairs to specific claim identifiers for claim‑level analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alice Decision Flag (alice_in)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates if the form paragraph and/or text in the action references the Supreme Court decision in Alice Corp. v. CLS Bank International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify Office actions referencing Alice; useful when analyzing 101/judicial exception citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilski Decision Flag (bilski_in)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates if the form paragraph and/or text in the action references the Supreme Court decision in Bilski v. Kappos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies Office actions that reference Bilski; helps detect invocation of that decision in 101 analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayo Decision Flag (mayo_in)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates if the form paragraph and/or text in the action references the Supreme Court decision in Mayo v. Prometheus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for tracking Mayo references in subject‑matter eligibility rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Myriad Decision Flag (myriad_in)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates if the form paragraph and/or text in the action references the Supreme Court decision in Association for Molecular Pathology v. Myriad Genetics, Inc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies references to Myriad in Office actions (relevant for DNA/genetic subject matter eligibility issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Patent or Pre‑grant Publication Citation (citation_pat_pgpub_id)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains references cited in prosecution of the application, predominantly U.S. patent grants or U.S. pre‑grant publications; for a small subset may include raw text extracted from an Office action (including foreign patent documents or non‑patent literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the raw citation field used to derive parsed identifiers; foreign doc formats and NPL are inconsistently formatted and often not parsed in this release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsed Citation (parsed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains the U.S. patent grant number or U.S. pre‑grant publication number parsed from citation_pat_pgpub_id (may also contain foreign patent document numbers if present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parsed for stable linking of citations; parsing may be imperfect for foreign and NPL citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 892 Source Flag (form892)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether the prior U.S. patent grant or U.S. pre‑grant publication citation was retrieved from Form PTO‑892 (Notices of References Cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO‑892 captures citations recorded by the examiner; form892 marks that source for each citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 1449 Source Flag (form1449)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether the prior U.S. patent grant or U.S. pre‑grant publication citation was retrieved from Form PTO‑1449 (Information Disclosure Statement submitted by applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may submit multiple Forms PTO‑1449 during prosecution; form1449 flags applicant‑submitted prior art. Note: citation data from this source may be incomplete for applications still pending as of July 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation Referenced in Office Action (citation_in_oa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates whether the citation was referenced in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When positive, the fields ifw_number, action_type, and action_subtype will identify the relevant Office action and rejection grounds for which the citation is referenced, enabling linking between citations and document‑actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 101 Ontology and Action Subtype Labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: A basic 35 U.S.C. 101 ontology is created using MPEP categorizations (double patenting, subject matter eligibility, utility, improper naming of inventor) and then refined into 12 action subtype labels based on training materials, exam memos, form paragraphs, and significant Supreme Court decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial categorization is by keyword/phrase queries of 101 rejection text; when multiple subtypes apply, prioritize Supreme Court decisions (reverse temporal order) then keywords. Also generate binary fields indicating whether each of four Supreme Court decisions (Alice, Bilski, Mayo, Myriad) were mentioned to capture multiple applicable decisions. Action subtype labels are in Appendix C mapping search terms to labels. Labels are intended as an initial attempt and not authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA Mapping for Action Subtypes (102/112 pre/post‑AIA mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the Leahy‑Smith America Invents Act (AIA) amended certain statutory sections, action subtypes for 102 and labels for 112 are mapped to provide consistency across pre‑ and post‑AIA texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: two pre‑AIA 102 paragraphs (102(a) and 102(b)) correspond to AIA subparagraph 102(a)(1); pre‑AIA 102(e) maps to 102(a)(2). For 112, pre‑AIA paragraphs are mapped to alphabetical post‑AIA equivalents (a–f) to produce consistent action_subtype labels across the dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset File Structure (office_actions, rejections, citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The release consists of three data files: office_actions (4.4M observations, each an Office action), rejections (10.1M document‑action pairs), and citations (58.9M unique application‑citation pairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: office_actions contains indicators for action types and document metadata; rejections contains action_type/action_subtype and claim mapping; citations contains parsed citations plus flags indicating source and whether cited in an Office action. Use the ifw_number and action_type/action_subtype to link across files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known Data Limitations and Coverage Flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Documented limitations such as typographical/input errors, missing Office actions for some applications, inability to parse many foreign patent document and non‑patent literature citations, and lag between filing and Office action mailing dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should merge this Dataset with other sources (e.g., PatEx, Public PAIR, Patent Claims Research Dataset) to obtain filing dates, continuation history, prosecution events, and claim text. Coverage varies by filing year and cohort; first‑action allowances are not captured (no Non‑Final/Final rejection issued).
